title: Add connection
pickHint: Choose the type of database to connect to.

fields.name: Name
fields.projectHint: Saved in the repository's .spelaion/ folder and shared through git. Passwords are never written to it.
fields.personalHint: Saved only on this computer, in your personal settings folder.
fields.noTunnelsHint: No tunnels yet: create one with “New tunnel…”.
fields.fileHint: An existing file, or a new empty one from “New database…”. Inside the repository the path is stored relative to it.
fields.mcpHint: Agents using spelaiondb mcp can only read, and every query is audited.
fields.mcpWriteHint: Agents can run one write at a time (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE with WHERE, CREATE or ALTER of tables, views and indexes…), each in its own transaction. DROP, TRUNCATE, changes to every row, procedures and permissions are always refused, and everything is audited.
fields.mcpProdWarning: This is a production connection: agents will be able to change its data.
fields.tlsHint: With “Verify”, an empty certificate field uses the system’s trusted certificates.
fields.tunnelHint: The database is reached through the tunnel’s last hop.
fields.fixedLocationHint: When editing, the connection stays in the same file and folder.
fields.serverFileHint: Its path on the tunnel's last hop. SpelaionDB runs that server's sqlite3 (3.37 or later, in its safe mode): the file is never copied.
fields.useTunnelForFile: The file is on a server: open it there through an SSH tunnel
fields.tunnelForFileHint: The last hop must allow running commands (not only port forwarding) and have sqlite3 installed.
fields.localPortHint: Fixed port on 127.0.0.1 where the tunnel listens for this connection, so other tools can use it too. Empty: any free port (or one from the range in Settings → Network).
fields.tlsCertPlaceholder: Empty: log in with the authentication method
fields.clientCertHint: Logs in with a certificate instead of a password (the server must accept it for this user). The key stays on your computer: keep it in your personal folder, never in the repository.

tls.prefer: Prefer (encrypt if the server allows it)
tls.verify-full: Verify the authority and the host name

test.passwordRequired: Enter the password to test the connection.

auth.savedHint: The password goes to the system keychain (Credential Manager, Keychain or Secret Service), never to the connection file.
auth.askHint: Not saved: it will be asked each time you connect. The password typed here is only used to test.
auth.envHint: Read from this variable when connecting; the file only stores its name.
auth.otherHint: This password comes from a reference the form cannot edit (1Password, a command or a named keychain entry). It is kept as is; edit the file to change it.
auth.keepPlaceholder: Leave empty to keep the saved password

filterHint: Patterns separated by commas: * is any run of characters, ? one character, \ escapes the next one; case is ignored. Without include patterns everything is included; exclude patterns hide what matches them.
filterPersonal: Filters are yours: they are saved on this computer, not in the connection's file, and only change what the explorer shows.
deleteExplanation: {{name}} will be removed: its file {{file}} is deleted, along with its password in the system keychain if one was saved.
deleteProjectHint: It is a project connection, shared through git: your team will lose it too when you commit the change.
deletePersonalHint: It is a personal connection: only this computer is affected.
deleteBusy: A query is running or connecting on it. Stop it first.

tunnel.name: Tunnel name
tunnel.nameHint: Connections refer to the tunnel by this name.
tunnel.fixedHint: When editing, the tunnel keeps its name and location: connections refer to it.
tunnel.agentKey: Only this key from the agent (optional)
tunnel.agentKeyPlaceholder: Empty: every key loaded in the agent

methodHints.agent: Uses the keys loaded in your SSH agent; choose one if the server limits authentication attempts.
methodHints.key: If the key has a passphrase, it is asked when connecting.
methodHints.password: Typed once to save it in the keychain, or asked each time.
methodHints.keyboard-interactive: For servers that ask questions such as a 2FA code: they are asked when connecting.
methodHints.custom: These methods are tried in order and kept as they are in the file.

tunnel.keepaliveHint: When a server sends nothing for that long, a keep-alive is sent, so a NAT or firewall does not drop an idle tunnel; after that many unanswered the tunnel is shown as down. Empty: 15 s and 3. 0 seconds sends none; 0 unanswered never gives up.
tunnel.connectTimeoutHint: How long each hop may take to answer before giving up. Empty: 15 s. Time spent typing a passphrase or a 2FA code does not count.

url.label: Or paste a connection URL
url.unsupported: This app has no driver for that database yet.

dbeaver.or: Or bring your connections from another client:
dbeaver.title: Import from DBeaver
dbeaver.savePasswords: Store the passwords DBeaver saved in the system keychain
dbeaver.passwordsHint: Otherwise SpelaionDB asks for them when connecting. Passwords are never written to the connection files. SSH tunnels are imported too.

kubernetes.name: Resource name
kubernetes.noPorts: The resource declares no ports: type the port in the Main tab.
kubernetes.hint: SpelaionDB runs kubectl port-forward with your kubeconfig. The connection’s port is the port of this resource; the host in the Main tab is only used for TLS.
kubernetes.exclusive: A connection goes through Kubernetes or an SSH tunnel, not both.
kubernetes.mainHint: Through Kubernetes: the port is the resource’s, chosen in the Kubernetes tab.

cloudToken.awsRdsHint: Runs “aws rds generate-db-auth-token” on every connection: the AWS CLI must be signed in on this computer. Tokens last 15 minutes and need TLS.
cloudToken.azureAdHint: Runs “az account get-access-token” on every connection: the Azure CLI must be signed in on this computer. Use your Entra ID user as the user.
cloudToken.googleCloudSqlHint: Runs “gcloud sql generate-login-token” on every connection: the gcloud CLI must be signed in on this computer. Use your IAM user as the user.
